title: Header Extras
description: Schema for the BricksExtras 'Header Extras' settings group, injected into page settings and header/content-template settings via the builder/settings/page/controls_data and builder/settings/template/controls_data filters. Not an element — there is no live schema ability for this group (bricks/list-settings-schema covers Bricks core global settings only, and bricks/get-page-settings / bricks/get-template-settings return an opaque stored-values object with no field metadata). This file is hand-derived from includes/BricksExtrasHeaderExtras.php and is the only schema source for this settings group — keep it in sync with that file's extras_header_builder_options(), extras_header(), and extras_header_attributes() methods if the plugin version changes.

notes.precedence: get_current_template_setting() resolves each key independently: page settings first (if the key literally exists in page settings, even as an empty/false value, it wins and short-circuits — see the isset()/array_key_exists() check), then content template settings (only if truthy), then header template settings (only if truthy), then the PHP-side runtime default. This means a page-level key set to an empty/false value can still 'win' over a truthy content/header template value, unlike the two lower tiers which only apply when truthy.
notes.breakpointOptions: xOverlayHeader and xStickyHeaderAbove share the same dynamically-built options list: one entry per site's registered Bricks breakpoint (\Bricks\Breakpoints::$breakpoints, keyed by numeric width, labeled '{label} ( > {width+1}px )'), plus two synthetic values 'none' and 'always'. Breakpoint widths are site-specific (this site's registered breakpoints at time of writing: desktop/1279 (base), tablet_portrait/991, mobile_landscape/767, mobile_portrait/478) — always confirm current values via bricks/get-design-context (breakpoints field) rather than assuming these, since custom breakpoints are enabled per-site.
notes.checkboxGotcha: xStickyHeaderScroll and xStickyHeaderHide are rendered as a select control ('true'/'false' string options), not a real Bricks checkbox — but disableHeader-style true/false semantics elsewhere in this plugin/Bricks core are often read via isset() rather than by value, so never assume 'setting a boolean-looking field to false' is equivalent to removing/disabling it without checking the specific consuming code. For the fields in this schema specifically, both PHP consumption points do a strict '=== "true"' string check, so explicitly writing 'false' does correctly disable them (unlike the unrelated disableHeader page-setting checkbox this plugin also has, which is read via isset() and requires key removal, not a false value, to disable).

xOverlayHeaderSep.label: Overlay Header
xOverlayHeaderSep.description: Position the header over the top of the first section and remove header row background colors
xOverlayHeaderSep.note: Not a real setting — a visual section divider in the builder UI only. No corresponding key is ever read or written.

xOverlayHeader.label: Breakpoint

valueSchema.description: '<breakpoint-width>' is a literal numeric string matching one of this site's registered Bricks breakpoint widths, e.g. "991".

xOverlayHeader.runtimeDefaultBehavior: Unset/falsy is treated as 'none' at read time (extras_header() line ~249: `(bool) get_current_template_setting('xOverlayHeader') ? ... : 'none'`), which disables overlay mode entirely — no CSS is emitted, no data-x-overlay gating applies visually.
xOverlayHeader.mechanism: 'none' → overlay CSS never emitted. 'always' → overlay CSS emitted unwrapped (applies at every viewport width). A breakpoint width → overlay CSS is wrapped in `@media only screen and (min-width: {width+1}px)`. This is CSS media-query gating, server-rendered via wp_add_inline_style — not a JS runtime comparison (contrast with xStickyHeaderAbove below).

xHeaderZindex.label: z-index
xHeaderZindex.runtimeDefaultBehavior: Unset/falsy → the #brx-header z-index rule is omitted entirely from the generated inline CSS (no fallback value written).

xStickyHeaderSep.label: Sticky header
xStickyHeaderSep.note: Not a real setting — visual divider only.

xStickyHeaderScroll.label: Enable
xStickyHeaderScroll.runtimeDefaultBehavior: Read via strict `'true' === get_current_template_setting('xStickyHeaderScroll')` in both extras_header() and extras_header_attributes() — unset, empty, or any value other than the exact string 'true' behaves as disabled. This is the master switch every other xSticky* setting below depends on; none of them have any effect while this is not exactly 'true'.
xStickyHeaderScroll.note: Despite looking like a boolean, this is a string-valued select control, not a checkbox — the value must be the literal string 'true', not a JSON boolean true, to activate (mirrors how the ability layer round-trips it, e.g. observed live as the string "true" via bricks/get-template-settings).

xStickyHeaderAbove.label: Breakpoint

valueSchema.description: Same dynamic breakpoint-width option set as xOverlayHeader above.

xStickyHeaderAbove.runtimeDefaultBehavior: **No schema default is set, and unset/falsy is read as literal 'none' at runtime** (extras_header_attributes() line ~410: `get_current_template_setting('xStickyHeaderAbove') ? intval(...) + 1 : 'none'`), written into the header's `data-x-break` HTML attribute as the string "none". The frontend header.js reads that attribute as `mediaWidth` and gates all sticky activation on `window.innerWidth >= mediaWidth` — comparing a number against the string "none" coerces to NaN, and any comparison against NaN is always false. Net effect: xStickyHeaderScroll can be exactly 'true', xStickyHeaderScrollDistance can be correctly set, and sticky will still never activate at any viewport width, with no error anywhere — until xStickyHeaderAbove is explicitly set. Set to 'always' for the common 'just make it sticky' case, or a specific breakpoint width to gate by viewport.
xStickyHeaderAbove.severity: high — this is the most common way sticky silently does nothing despite every other setting being correct and persisted.

xStickyHeaderScrollDistance.label: Scroll distance (px)
xStickyHeaderScrollDistance.info: Distance scrolled down the page before header becomes sticky
xStickyHeaderScrollDistance.runtimeDefaultBehavior: Unset/falsy → written as data-x-scroll="0" (sticky-active triggers immediately on any scroll, once xStickyHeaderAbove actually allows activation).

xStickyHeaderZindex.label: Sticky z-index
xStickyHeaderZindex.runtimeDefaultBehavior: Unset/falsy → effective value falls back to 999 in the generated CSS (`#brx-header.x-header_sticky-active { z-index: 999; }`) — this one genuinely has a working fallback, matching its placeholder.

xStickyHeaderFadeDuration.label: Duration (Header)
xStickyHeaderFadeDuration.runtimeDefaultBehavior: Unset/falsy → CSS custom property --x-header-fade-transition is set to '0' (no transition duration, instant fade).

xStickyHeaderTransitionDuration.label: Duration (Header row)
xStickyHeaderTransitionDuration.runtimeDefaultBehavior: Unset/falsy → CSS custom property --x-header-transition is set to '0' (no transition duration, instant).

xHideHeaderSep.label: Hide Header
xHideHeaderSep.description: Hide the sticky header after scrolling a certain distance
xHideHeaderSep.note: Not a real setting — visual divider only.

xStickyHeaderHide.label: Hide header after scrolling
xStickyHeaderHide.runtimeDefaultBehavior: Read via strict `'true' === get_current_template_setting('xStickyHeaderHide')`. Independent of xStickyHeaderScroll's own default — but has no effect at all unless xStickyHeaderScroll is also exactly 'true', since the entire hide-header code branch lives inside the sticky-enabled branch of extras_header_attributes().
xStickyHeaderHide.note: A second, independent behavior layered on top of sticky (Headroom.js-based) — not a duplicate enable switch for sticky itself. See the SKILL.md 'Never do' note.

xStickyHeaderHideEffect.label: Animation
xStickyHeaderHideEffect.runtimeDefaultBehavior: Unset/falsy → effective value falls back to 'slideUp' (data-x-hide-effect attribute) — a working fallback.

xStickyHeaderHideTollerance.label: Tolerance (px)
xStickyHeaderHideTollerance.runtimeDefaultBehavior: Unset/falsy → written as data-x-header-tollerance="0". Note the misspelling ('Tollerance') is the real control key, not a typo to correct when writing settings.
xStickyHeaderHideTollerance.note: Field key is genuinely spelled 'xStickyHeaderHideTollerance' (double-L) in the plugin source — do not 'correct' it to 'Tolerance' when writing settings, the key must match exactly.

xOverlayHeaderApply.label: Apply
xOverlayHeaderApply.note: Not a real setting — a builder-UI-only apply/reload button control type. No corresponding key is ever read or written.
